Features

Everything an AI team needs to do real work

These capabilities ship in the beta. Items marked as needing setup require your own account or service.

AI agent teams

Create bots with their own roles and group them to work on one task together. Each bot keeps its own history, working folder and tools.

Many models and providers

AIKING Core with Claude, plus the Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini, Grok, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras and MiniMax engines and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint — local models included.

Marketplace

Install ready-made agents such as Media Producer, Ad Strategist, Trend Scout and Research Analyst, and skills for TikTok hooks, campaign briefs and meeting notes. Update or remove with one click.

Skills and plugins (MCP)

Extend bots with reviewed skills and MCP servers over stdio, HTTP or SSE. Tools with side effects always wait for your approval.

Workspace and files

Bots work in the folder you choose and read or create files, images and documents. Encrypted backup restores the whole workspace on a new machine.

Schedules

Run a bot once or on a schedule: a Monday morning report, a daily trend scan, a weekend inbox digest.

Remote work

Sign in with your email to open your workspace on a computer or in a browser, no pairing code needed. Workspace owners invite members and set their role, and can revoke access at any time.

Voice calls with bots Needs setup

Talk to your agents: pick a microphone and speaker, interrupt naturally, reconnect automatically. The app checks the engine, microphone and speech service first and tells you exactly what to connect if something is missing.

How it works

Four steps to a working bot team

  1. 1

    Download

    Get the Windows installer straight from the AIKINGBOT server and install it in a minute, no administrator rights needed.

  2. 2

    Connect

    Sign in with your email and a one-time code, pick your workspace, then press Connect to sign in to Codex, Claude Code or another engine with the provider's own account login.

  3. 3

    Build your team

    Pick agents from the Marketplace or create new bots, and give each one a model, skills and a working folder.

  4. 4

    Delegate

    Send a task, set a schedule or start a voice call. Follow progress, approve tools and get results right in the conversation.

Install

  1. Download AIKINGBOT-…-setup.exe above.
  2. Open the file. The beta is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may warn you: choose "More info" → "Run anyway".
  3. AIKINGBOT installs for your Windows account and opens. Use it on this computer, or choose "Sign in to your workspace" to sign in with your email.
  4. In your workspace, open Settings → AI and press Connect on an engine; the app installs what it needs and opens the provider's official sign-in page.

Updates

From the first beta with an update channel, AIKINGBOT checks for new versions at start-up and every hour, downloads in the background and shows a restart button to finish. Accounts, bots, skills and workspaces are kept. You can also check manually in Settings → About.

Verify the file

In PowerShell, run the command below and compare it with the SHA-256 shown above:

Get-FileHash .\AIKINGBOT-setup.exe -Algorithm SHA256
FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Does AIKINGBOT cost anything?

The app is free during the beta. AI usage is billed by the model provider: use the ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Grok plan you already have, a pay-as-you-go API key, or a free local model.

Which models can I use?

AIKING Core uses Claude through an Anthropic API key. The app also keeps the Claude, ChatGPT/Codex, Gemini, Grok, Mistral, Groq, Cerebras and MiniMax engines and OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Each bot can use a different model.

Where is my data stored?

On your computer, in the .aikingbot folder of your Windows account. With an AIKINGBOT server, the remote workspace data lives on that server. Content is only sent to the model provider you choose for each conversation turn.

What computer do I need?

Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit, about 1 GB of free disk space and an Internet connection for cloud models. Linux builds (.deb, AppImage) exist too; macOS comes later.

What is the AIKINGBOT server for?

The server runs the same backend as the desktop app so bots keep working 24/7, lets you open the web app in a browser, pair several devices and share workspaces. The desktop app also works on its own without a server.

Can a bot run dangerous commands on its own?

No. Tools with side effects need your approval, and dangerous tools are refused unless you explicitly allow them. Remote devices pair with one-time codes, get scoped permissions and can be revoked. Voice never approves a tool.

What are the beta limitations?

The installer is not code-signed yet, so Windows warns on first install. The in-app interface is English for now; Vietnamese comes later. Voice calls need configured STT/TTS services. Composio OAuth connections need your own account. Back up important workspaces.

Will updating delete my data?

No. An update replaces the program only; data in .aikingbot is kept and migrated when needed. An older version refuses to open data written by a newer one to avoid corruption.

Ready for your own AI team?

Download the Windows Beta, connect the model you already use and hand over your first task in minutes.
